title: Every valid CUDA execution path of one tiny 3D problem against its CPU float64 solution

fixture.problem: 3D Yee grid 20 x 18 x 16 cells, uniform 0.1 um mesh, 4 CPML cells on every face (Bloch pair on y for the complex cells), one index-1.5 sphere, one Ez point source with a one-cycle pulse, one Ez point monitor and one x-normal plane DFT monitor with three frequency points

fields: complex (fixed Bloch phase on y: complex E/H state and complex DFT accumulators)
stream: side torch.cuda.Stream around the whole run

adjoint_axes.loss: sum of squared signal magnitudes over every step and monitor
adjoint_axes.epsilon: the voxelized sphere scene as a (Nx, Ny, Nz) tensor with requires_grad

fixture.cuda_budget: one 20 x 18 x 16 grid per cell, well below the 32^3 limit of the shared RTX 3060

reference_method: the same discrete problem run by Simulation with backend='cpu' and precision='float64' (the numpy Yee/CPML backend of the fdtd grid package) for the forward matrix, and by DifferentiableSimulation on a CPU float64 epsilon (torch CPU forward, torch explicit transpose) for the adjoint matrix; this is a layer-A discrete comparison of backends, not an independent physics oracle

observables.name: electric
observables.definition: final E field divided by max |E_ref|

observables.name: magnetic
observables.definition: final H field divided by max |H_ref|

observables.name: signals
observables.definition: point monitor time trace divided by max |signal_ref|

observables.name: plane DFT fields
observables.definition: complex plane DFT samples divided by max |field_ref|

observables.name: plane flux
observables.definition: plane flux per frequency divided by max |flux_ref|

observables.name: epsilon gradient
observables.definition: d loss / d epsilon divided by max |gradient_ref|

observables.name: backend report
observables.definition: summary.cuda_kernel, cuda_monitor_kernel, cuda_graph, precision, complex_fields and report.forward_backend, backward_backend must name the path that ran

acceptance.comparison: numpy.testing.assert_allclose on the normalized observables, elementwise |got - ref| <= atol + rtol |ref|
acceptance.rejection_policy: complex fields with cuda_kernel='fused' raise ValueError 'The fused CUDA kernel currently supports real fields'; complex fields with cuda_monitor_kernel='fused' raise ValueError 'Fused frequency monitors require real CUDA fields'; backward_kernel='fused' on CPU raises ValueError 'fused backward requires a CUDA tensor'; a fused backward with PMC faces raises ValueError 'does not implement PMC'; a fused kernel on the CPU backend raises ValueError; cuda_graph_steps outside 1..64 or above 1 without graphs raises ValueError. No silent fallback is accepted
acceptance.documented_contract: DifferentiableSimulation runs the fused kernel for every real CUDA forward regardless of Region.cuda_kernel (DIFFERENTIABLE_FDTD.md); the adjoint cells assert the reported forward backend instead of treating this as a fallback
acceptance.pilot_note: a design pilot on 2026-09-22 before this declaration measured normalized deviations of at most 1.6e-6 (float32) and 2.1e-15 (float64) on this fixture; the declared limits are the program thresholds, not the pilot values

not_yet_covered: the same matrix on a second, independently installed CUDA platform (RTX 5880 Ada): prepared, not run here

notes: Runs on the shared RTX 3060 with a 5760-cell grid. Bitwise identity between the default and a side stream is asserted separately by G4-03; here each stream cell is judged against the CPU reference only.
